title: segmented-tenant-coalescer-with-multi-key-invalidation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The embeddings/reranking endpoint is seeing increased tail latency and variable cost per query for multi-tenant workloads due to redundant embedding computation and poor cache invalidation boundary handling. This ticket implements a segmented tenant-aware coalescing cache that supports multi-key (document id + prefix hash + content-hash) deduplication and configurable invalidation policies so we can reduce redundant embedding work, lower p99 latency, and bound memory usage per tenant.

Scope: engineering work to introduce a new cache layer in the embedding service, migration plan for the existing cache entries, instrumentation, API flags for rollout, and regression tests. Not changing public API surface for customers; internal routing/lookup will be transparent.

Goals: reduce embedding compute by >=35% on dedup-friendly workloads, improve median latency by 10-20ms, and keep p99 within existing SLOs during rollout.
technical_details:
Design summary: 1) Sharded per-tenant cache namespaces to prevent noisy neighbor eviction; 2) Entry keys composed of three parts: tenant-id, prefix-fingerprint (first N tokens normalized), and content-hash (sha256 of canonicalized text). The cache supports two lookup modes in order: exact content-hash -> prefix-fingerprint fallback -> routing to compute. 3) Coalescer: in-flight request dedup table keyed by content-hash to collapse concurrent computes. 4) Eviction: tiered LRU with weight based on token-length and recency; ability to pin small vectors (<=128 tokens) for high-frequency tenants. 5) Invalidation policy: support tag-based invalidation (doc-version tag), time-ttl, and cohort-based rolling invalidation for large dataset updates. 6) Persistence: use existing Redis cluster with prefix shard keys; metadata kept for TTL and origin. 7) Metrics: hit/miss by lookup-mode, cost-saved estimate, evicted-by, pin-rate.

Implementation notes: - Add new cache adapter module (embed_cache/coalescer_v2) with pluggable keying strategy. - Maintain backward compatibility: a feature flag EMBED_CACHE_V2 to switch to new keying in controlled rollout. - Provide migration script: backfill prefix fingerprints for hot keys and compute content-hash for candidates using a sampling job. - Include throttling: max_coalesced_inflight per-tenant to avoid memory storms.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (canary): enable EMBED_CACHE_V2 for 2 internal tenants and synthetic load. Observe hit-rate and tail latencies for 48 hours. Phase 1: enable for 10% of tenant traffic via routing config and monitor; fail closed to legacy cache on regressions. Phase 2: increase to 50% with gradual eviction tuning; run backfill to populate prefix fingerprints for most-frequent keys. Phase 3: full flip with deprecation window for legacy cache (30 days).

Rollback: flip flag off. If regressions detected, auto-fallback on routing layer to legacy cache for affected tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests for coalescer and multi-key lookup pass in CI
Canary tenants show improved duplicate compute reduction (>=20% reduction) within 48h without SLO regressions
Instrumentation emits new cache metrics and dashboard updated with hit/miss and dedupe ratios
No customer-facing API changes; verified by E2E calls matching baseline outputs
Migration/backfill job runs without causing Redis CPU/memory spikes; documented prerequisites
testing_plan:
- Local integration harness with synthetic corpus to simulate prefix-sharing and near-duplicate content.
- Loadtest in staging with traffic mix (80% read, 20% updates) to validate eviction and invalidation behavior.
- Chaos test: simulate rapid doc-version invalidations for a tenant and assert system stability and invalidation latency <5s.
- Regression test against reranking pipeline to ensure embedding vector stability and downstream ranker metrics don't regress beyond small noise.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Dashboards: cache-overview per-tenant, lookup-mode breakdown, coalesced-inflight count, evictions-per-minute, avg-token-weighted-size. Alerts: 1) cache-miss-rate > 30% sustained for 30m on canary tenants, 2) evictions > baseline*3 for 10m, 3) redis-memory-pressure > 80%, 4) coalesced-inflight > threshold leading to OOM risk.
Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/embed-cache-failures
comments: 2025-02-12 Maya Chen: Created ticket after postmortem on rerank tail latency spike. Initial design reviewed with DS and SRE; decision to move to multi-keying rather than single fingerprint to reduce false positives in dedupe.

2025-02-14 Omar Patel: Prototyped coalescer module and benchmarked in local cluster. Results: single-node CPU time for dedup reduction ~42% for sampled queries; Redis ops increased by ~8%. Need to cap per-tenant coalesced_inflight to prevent memory spikes.

2025-02-16 Priya Singh (SRE): Concern: backfill job may overwhelm Redis if run across all tenants. Recommendation: staged backfill per-tenant with throttled workers and rate limit writes; provide a dry-run to estimate write volume.

2025-02-18 Nora Blake (DS): Quality check: content-hash canonicalization removed punctuation and normalized whitespace. Found 2% false-positive collisions with naive truncation. Agreed to use full sha256 + 64-bit prefix in index to reduce collision risk.

2025-02-20 Alex Ramos (PM): Approving moving to canary after SRE mitigations (worker rate-limits, per-tenant memory caps) are implemented. Action: create canary runbook and schedule 48h observation window.
2025-02-20 Omar Patel: Feature flag EMBED_CACHE_V2 implemented; canary config prepared. Next: run migration dry-run and spin up canary tenants.
notes: Trade-offs: Choosing content-hash primary reduces duplicate computes but increases Redis key cardinality and write amplification during backfill. We mitigate by targeted backfill and per-tenant caps. Future work: evaluate vector similarity dedupe to catch semantically equivalent docs, but that requires more compute and is out of scope for this cycle.
next_steps: 1) Finish backfill dry-run and implement staged worker throttling (Omar). 2) Add per-tenant coalesced_inflight limits with metric exports (Priya). 3) Prepare canary tenants and schedule canary window (Alex).
estimated_savings: Projected 35% reduction in redundant embedding compute for dedupe-friendly tenants, ~12% avg cost reduction across platform if rollout completes as planned.
audits_and_compliance: No PII changes. Audit note: record invalidation events in structured log to satisfy traceability requirements for Private deployments. Implementation will include an opt-in flag for Private customers to enable event forwarding to their KMS-backed audit pipeline.
